_comment: Eden's OWN acquisition, not a client's. Added 2026-08-26 so Eden's ad spend sits alongside the clients' in the same reporting rather than only in Ads Manager. EDEN the agent is the system's brain; 'eden' the client is the business buying its own ads.

market._comment: Eden is based in Montreal and the ad account bills in CAD, but the live ad set targets the US — Eden sells to US real estate teams. Do not assume the audience geo matches the business geo here.

meta._comment: Deliberately EMPTY. Meta's HOUSING category covers ads for listings, home sales/rentals, mortgages and homeowners insurance. Eden sells a marketing system TO real estate agents — the audience is realtors, the product is B2B software and services, and no housing is being offered. Real-estate-ADJACENT is not the same as real estate. The 3% config is HOUSING for the opposite reason: that client actually sells homes.
meta.pixelNote: EDEN Base Funnel Dataset. Installed inside the GoHighLevel form iframe on edenmtl.com/get-started/, NOT on the parent page. Meta therefore sees the Lead event but never the landing-page view, the fbclid lands on edenmtl.com where the iframe cannot read it, and Safari/iOS third-party cookie blocking hits iframe pixels hardest. Conversions will under-report until the base code is also on the page itself.

forge._comment: Grounded in Eden's own history, which is thin. Only one campaign has meaningful spend: Realtor Acquisition (March 2025), $1,888 over 1,694 clicks — CTR 2.64%, CPC $1.11, a strong CTR for cold B2B. Lead data is far weaker: 3 leads on $19.43 of spend in the Conversions API campaign, which is too small to set a threshold from.
forge.cplThresholdNote: UNVALIDATED and deliberately loose. The only observed CPL is ~$6.48 from a 3-lead sample, which is not credible for a booked call with a real estate team. Eden's own deal size is large enough that a three-figure CPL can still be profitable, so a tight threshold would pause working ads. Revisit after 20-30 real leads.
forge.roasNote: DISABLED. Eden does not record deal value per lead anywhere the system can read, so ROAS would compute as null forever. A rule that cannot fire looks like coverage that does not exist.
forge.dailyBudgetCapNote: Campaign budget is $50/day (CBO, set at campaign level). 75 leaves headroom to scale without letting a runaway through.
forge.fatigueThresholdNote: Frequency is impressions/reach so it is always >= 1; the 0.7 that shipped in the other configs was impossible to satisfy and flagged everything. 3.0 sits above normal operation.

ghl._comment: Connected 2026-08-26. Five pipelines exist; Main Pipeline is the one carrying real opportunities and the only one whose stages describe money (Placeholder Paid, Trial Client, Closed, EDEN System Subscribed). Cold SMS and Cold Voicemail Drop are outbound prospecting, not inbound ad leads.

outcomeStages._comment: INFERRED from stage names, not confirmed by Jacob — worth a check. Applies the same rule he set for the clients: won means money banked, active means committed but not yet banked. 'Trial Client' and 'Placeholder Paid' are real commitments that have not converted to full revenue, so they are active rather than won. 'Appointment Booked' is deliberately NOT active — for Eden a booked call is not a commitment, it is a conversation.

ghl.attributionNote: All nine attribution fields now exist in the location — six were already there, and meta_campaign_id / meta_adset_id / meta_ad_id were provisioned on 2026-08-26. They stay empty until the landing page captures fbclid and the Meta ad set carries {{campaign.id}}/{{adset.id}}/{{ad.id}} in its URL parameters.

quarry._comment: Quarry prospects Montreal small businesses with absent or dated websites, builds them a speculative site, and opens a screenshot-first SMS sequence. Eden's own acquisition, same as the forge block above. Search queries drive BOTH discovery and category assignment — Google Places types are too coarse to pick a design brief from, so the query that surfaced a business decides which brief it gets.
quarry.enabledNote: OFF until Jacob confirms the per-API spend and the Lovable plan credit ceiling. Every billable call in this agent checks this flag first.

discovery.recheckAfterDaysNote: How long a place_id stays skipped before it is looked at again. Google Places terms restrict how long its content may be cached — check the current policy before raising this. 30 days is the figure their terms have historically used for most content.
discovery.maxLeadsPerRunNote: Hard ceiling on generations per run, because each one burns Lovable credits. Raise only alongside the plan.

triage.visionScoreThresholdNote: A site that passes every technical check but scores >= 6 for looking dated still qualifies. This is the branch that catches a technically-fine site that looks like 2009.

phone.cacheDaysNote: A business line type effectively never changes. Long cache because each lookup is billable.
phone.voipPolicyNote: Jacob decided 2026-08-26: work confirmed mobiles only, set everything else aside for now. holdout is what implements that — VOIP and unclassifiable numbers stay in quarry_leads with a holdoutReason and are simply not worked, rather than being deleted. Changing this to reject would discard them permanently; changing it to allow would text lines that may not receive SMS. Revisit if calibration shows the VOIP bucket is large, because some business VOIP does take SMS and a big bucket would mean real reachable volume sitting idle.
phone.enabledNote: Turned off 2026-08-27 — Jacob wants email as the main tool, not SMS. Phone verification (Twilio Lookup, $0.008/number) existed only to gate the SMS send path; with SMS off by default there is nothing for it to gate, so leaving it on would just spend money determining mobile status nobody acts on. Flip to true to bring SMS back — nothing else needs to change, since isMobile stays null on every lead while this is off and that alone is what keeps SMS candidates empty in send.ts.

generation.bookingUrlNote: GHL calendar link for the call CTA in the pitch email. REQUIRED now, not optional — the pitch has no other link in it. IMPORTANT: set this calendar's minimum scheduling notice (in GHL, the calendar's own settings — look for something like "minimum scheduling notice" or "appointments cannot be booked less than X in advance") to however many days Jacob actually needs to build a site by hand before the call happens, e.g. 5-7 business days. Without that, someone could book tomorrow and there would be nothing ready to show them.
generation._comment: Module 4 (Lovable site generation) is PAUSED as of 2026-08-27 — Jacob is building sites by hand himself for now, using the lead time between a booked call and the call itself. previewUrl/previewImageUrl on a lead will stay empty until this resumes; nothing in the outreach flow depends on them anymore.

outreach.dailySendCapNote: Deliverability/carrier-health measure, independent of any compliance requirement handled in GHL. Sends are spaced with jitter rather than fired as a burst.

templates.screenshot: Hi, this is {{senderName}} — I put together a quick site redesign for {{businessName}}, wanted you to see it. Want the live link to click around?
templates.link: Here it is — {{previewUrl}}. Have a look and tell me what you'd change.
templates.nudge: Hey, just checking if you got a chance to look — no pressure!

outreach.channelNote: SMS only. Email is captured for mobile leads as a second address on file, NOT as an outreach channel — there is no email sequence and building one is a separate decision with its own CASL posture.

email._comment: Cold email channel, added 2026-08-27. Reuses the exact same discovery/triage/enrichment as texting — "scrape businesses in an area" already happens in quarry.searches above; this just adds a second send channel for leads (mobile AND landline/VOIP) who have a published email. NOT wired to a live domain yet — fromDomain/fromAddress/physicalAddress are all blank on purpose. sendEmailBatch refuses to run until they are set; see EmailChannelNotConfiguredError in outreach.ts.
email.fromDomainNote: Set 2026-09-02. A subdomain built specifically for sending, not the root domain — correct move, keeps a burned cold-email domain from ever touching Jacob's real business domain. STILL NEEDS: verifying this in GHL under Settings > Email Services (adds SPF/DKIM DNS records at wherever this domain is registered) before any send will actually deliver.
email.physicalAddressNote: CASL requires a real mailing address in every commercial email. Left blank deliberately — do not invent one. sendEmailBatch throws until this is set.
email.dailySendCapNote: Deliberately low. A brand-new sending domain with no history gets flagged by spam filters almost immediately at real volume — inbox providers judge a domain by its early sending pattern, not just content. Ramp by roughly 50% a week (15 to ~25 to ~40) only after checking bounce/spam-complaint rates stay low; this number is a starting point; there is no auto-ramp built, it is a manual dial.

email.templatesNote: Updated 2026-08-27, three changes: (1) dropped "free" from the SUBJECT line specifically — it is a well-known spam-filter trigger word and this is a brand-new domain with no sending history, which is exactly the case that gets hurt most by it. Still says "free preview" in the body, where it is true and not scored the same way. (2) added {{context}} (rating/review count from Google, see contextLine()) right after the greeting for a second layer of specificity beyond {{problem}}. (3) added a reply as an equally valid alternative to the booking link everywhere — asking a stranger to book a call is a bigger first ask than asking them to hit reply, and a lot of small shop owners will find replying easier than a scheduling widget on their phone.
email.nudgeScheduleDaysNote: Two touches now, not one — [4, 10] means a first nudge at day 4 with no reply, a second at day 10. Most cold-email replies reportedly land after the FIRST follow-up, not the initial send, so a single-touch sequence was leaving real replies on the table.
email.replyFixNote: handleEmailReply now auto-sends the booking-link email (the new "booking" template) the moment someone replies positively — this is the fix for the exact failure mode in Jacob's old cold-SMS numbers: 342 people replied yes and almost none of them ever got a next step back. A positive reply must never just sit unanswered waiting for a human to notice.

ghlPipeline._comment: Built by hand in the GHL UI 2026-08-26 and verified live against location UJVzcdJ4NHJMhTs280OM. GHL v2 exposes no create-pipeline endpoint — same shape as the workflows.readonly limit in CLAUDE.md — so this pipeline can only be created and renamed by a human. These names are transcribed from the live pipeline, NOT chosen here: sync.ts matches them exactly and case-sensitively, so editing this list without editing GHL breaks the sync. The pipeline id is deliberately not stored; it is resolved by name at runtime.
ghlPipeline.name: Website Offer Pipeline
ghlPipeline.stagesNote: Screenshot Sent and Site Sent are deliberately separate — the offer turns on a picture going out first and the link only following a positive reply, so collapsing them would hide the one drop-off worth measuring. Note that Lost/Nurture merges two outcomes: a lead that said no and a lead worth re-touching later read identically in the funnel. Split it if the nurture path ever gets its own cadence.
